Bleu raises €5 million for demonstration-based factory robot learning

The claimed workflow takes about 20 minutes of demonstrations plus another 20 minutes before execution.

Humanoids Daily ↗29 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Funding product development

Paris-based Bleu Robotics raised €5 million in pre-seed funding led by Contrarian Ventures and OVNI Capital. Its software targets factories with frequent product and process changes. Initial industrial partners are lined up, while the product for routine deployment remains under development.

Understanding the timing

The co-founder describes roughly 20 minutes of handheld-gripper demonstrations and another 20 minutes before robot execution, about 40 minutes overall. Training and inference run onboard. Demonstrations use Unitree G1 and Franka hardware, but the turnaround remains a company claim.

Limits and business model

The approach incorporates pre-trained perception rather than learning everything from scratch. It focuses on rigid objects, excludes textiles for now and is designed to stop for help in unfamiliar situations. Autonomous travel between workstations remains future work. The proposed model is a per-robot monthly software subscription through manufacturers and integrators.
